messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT: p95 latency for /v1/generate crossed 1200ms in us-west-2 at 2024-06-15T14:00:10Z. Triggered routing policy evaluation and automatic fallback. Incident ID INC-20240615-42
clare-oncall: I'm seeing the same, paging on-call now. any quick wins?
sam-sre: grabbing this — checking router logs and switch events.
ryan-runtime: FYI I deployed a routing tweak at 13:58 UTC that enabled cross-model + regional fallback for spillover. could be related.
julia-infra: logs show repeated reroute events every ~30-45s, each reroute causes KV cache misses and cold-start overhead on fallback variants. looks like a feedback loop.
maya-cs: any visible customer impact? CS got 2 error reports from acct-omega about slow responses + a couple of 5xxs.
sam-sre: digging: the fallback variant 'gptx-8q-warm' has higher init latency under cold start. When the policy switches traffic to it, p95 spikes, which triggers the policy to reroute back -> oscillation.
clare-oncall: action: temporarily disable cross-model fallback for us-west-2 and increase hysteresis. we want to stop the rapid flips. sam can you apply config? :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
sam-sre: will do. patching policy now.
sam-sre: PATCH payload:
```
PATCH /api/v1/routing/policies/us-west-2
{
  "fallback_mode": "regional_only",
  "hysteresis_seconds": 300,
  "max_switches_per_minute": 1
}
```
sam-sre: policy applied, routing-service v=20240615-req1 reloaded.
incident-bot: NOTE: automatic reroute cooldown (hysteresis 300s) applied to policy us-west-2.
ryan-runtime: also pinning active model variant to avoid cross-model cold starts:
`redwoodctl route lock --region us-west-2 --model gptx-8b-v2 --duration 15m`
sam-sre: lock issued.
julia-infra: monitoring: p95 dropping back from ~1.4s to ~850ms in the last 3 minutes, no new reroute events seen.
maya-cs: letting acct-omega know, they reported improvements. they asked for a short summary.
clare-oncall: summary for customer: brief RC + mitigation steps and that we're doing a follow-up postmortem. thanks maya. :thumbsup: 
ryan-runtime: preliminary root cause: routing policy allowed cross-model switches with too-short hysteresis and allowed rapid multi-directional failovers (parallel fallback). combined with fallback variant cold starts -> p95-triggered flips. propose defaults: hysteresis 300s, single-switch-per-minute, and disable parallel cross-model fallback.
sam-sre: adding a runbook blurb: when p95-triggered reroute oscillation detected -> increase hysteresis, pin model variant, disable cross-model fallback, scale warm pool for fallback variants.
julia-infra: I'll own the postmortem and collect: policy diff, router switch timeline, KV cache miss rate, model warmup latencies, and affected customer logs.
clare-oncall: severity set to sev2. no active outage after mitigation but customer impact happened (transient 5xxs for acct-omega). Handing off to julia for 30m watch and postmortem.
julia-infra: ack, taking over at 14:35 UTC. I'll keep monitors at 1m granularity for the next hour.
clare-oncall: closing pager for now, monitoring window 1h. reopen if p95 > 1200ms sustained for 5m.
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-20240615-42: resolved -> mitigated (policy rollback + locks). Postmortem assigned to julia-infra.
sam-sre: created doc -> https://redwood.internal/docs/INC-20240615-42 (will add timeline + diffs).
clare-oncall: thanks everyone. follow-up actions: 1) revert or harden the 13:58 policy deploy, 2) add automated detection for reroute oscillation, 3) update default routing hysteresis.
julia-infra: noted, I'll include action owners and ETA in the postmortem.
